{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|Cuisine of the United States]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Date bars''' have crumbly upper and lower surfaces with a [[Cookbook:Date|date]] filling in the middle. Also see the [[Cookbook:Date Squares|Date Squares]] recipe.

==Ingredients==

*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*3 cups (1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]]) cut-up [[Cookbook:Date|dates]]
*1½ cup water
*¼ cup [[Cookbook:Shortening|shortening]]
*½ cup [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]]
*1 cup [[Cookbook:Brown Sugar|brown sugar]]
*½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
*1¾ cup [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]
*1½ cup quick-cooking [[Cookbook:Oatmeal|oatmeal]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]

==Procedure==

#Mix the dates, sugar, and water in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]].
#Cook over low heat, stirring constantly for about 10 minutes or until thickened. Cool.
#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] together the butter, shortening, and brown sugar in a separate container.
#Mix the flour, salt, baking soda, and oats into the crumble crust mix.
#Grease a 13x9-inch pan.
#Evenly press half of the crumble mixture into the bottom of the pan.
#Spread the date filling on top.
#Evenly place remaining crumble mixture into the pan, pressing lightly.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 25 to 30 minutes at [[Cookbook:Oven temperatures|400°F]], or until light brown.
#Cut into bars while still warm.
